name: Frankie Knuckles
claims: Resident DJ at the Warehouse from March 1977 (city landmark report).
Out gay man; Black gay club roots (Chicago LGBT Hall of Fame).
Part of the collective that created house; lone-inventor claims are DISPUTED.

name: Ron Hardy
dates: resident DJ from Feb 1983; death year disputed
claims: Resident DJ at the Music Box (earlier Den One).
Experimental mixing/editing pushed house harder and more psychedelic.
Club-tested Phuture's 'Acid Tracks.'
Death year DISPUTED (1991 vs 1992) - never state.

name: Robert Williams
claims: Founded/promoted the Warehouse; ran 'US Studios' parties.
First offered the Warehouse residency to Larry Levan (1976).
Rebranded the Warehouse as the Music Box (1983) and hired Ron Hardy.

name: Larry Levan
claims: Continental Baths resident; mentor/collaborator of Knuckles.
Declined the Warehouse residency; recommended Knuckles.

name: Jesse Saunders
claims: Co-created and pressed 'On & On' (Jes Say, Jan 1984) with Vince Lawrence.
Cassette club-testing preceded pressing.

name: Vince Lawrence
claims: Co-created and pressed 'On & On' with Saunders.
Wrote Farley's 'Love Can't Turn Around.'
Trax co-founder per some accounts (disputed).

name: Jamie Principle
claims: Wrote 'Your Love'; circulated it on cassette in clubs before vinyl.
Trax 1987 Knuckles-credited 'Your Love' reflects label practice, not authorship.

name: Marshall Jefferson
claims: 'Move Your Body' (1986) established the piano-led house anthem.
Co-produced Sleezy D's 'I've Lost Control' (1986).

name: Larry Heard (Mr. Fingers)
claims: Deep-house landmarks: 'Washing Machine,' 'Can You Feel It,' 'Beyond the Clouds.'
Fingers Inc. with Robert Owens brought songwriting into house.

name: Robert Owens
claims: Vocalist in Larry Heard's Fingers Inc. (with Ron Wilson).

name: Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk
claims: Leading house DJ; Hot Mix 5 member.
'Love Can't Turn Around' (1986) reached UK Top 10.

name: Darryl Pandy
claims: Gospel singer; vocal on Farley's 'Love Can't Turn Around.'

name: Phuture
claims: DJ Pierre, Spanky (Earl Smith Jr.), Herb J.
Recorded 'Acid Tracks' to tape; Hardy club-tested it at the Music Box.
Trax pressing 1987 credited with defining acid house.

name: Adonis
claims: Among first-wave producers whose tracks Hardy debuted at the Music Box.

name: Steve 'Silk' Hurley
claims: 'Jack Your Body' reported UK #1 (1987) - PROVISIONAL, single fan-wiki source.

name: Chip E.
claims: 'Jack Trax' (1985) cited as early-house-record candidate.

name: Wayne Williams
claims: Founded Chosen Few Disco Corp. (1977) with South Side DJs.
Has publicly questioned aspects of Jesse Saunders's account.

name: Celeste Alexander (DJ Celeste)
claims: One of Chicago's first female house DJs; Fantastic Four collective.

name: Lori Branch
claims: Early female house DJ from the Warehouse teen-party scene.

name: Lee Michaels
claims: WBMX program director; assembled the Hot Mix 5 in 1981.

name: Rocky Jones
claims: Co-founded DJ International with Benji Espinoza (1985).

name: Benji Espinoza
claims: Co-founded DJ International with Rocky Jones (1985).

name: Larry Sherman
claims: Credited as Trax Records co-founder; founding year and credits disputed.

name: Tadao Kikumoto
claims: Designed the Roland TB-303 (1981), TR-808 (1980), TR-909 (1983).

name: Steve Dahl
claims: WLUP DJ; promoted Disco Demolition Night (July 12, 1979).

name: The Warehouse
dates: period of significance 1977-1982; 206 S. Jefferson St.
claims: Members-only club founded/promoted by Robert Williams.
Frankie Knuckles resident from March 1977.
Black, Latino, largely gay crowd.
Term 'house music' derives from the club name; the recorded genre emerged later.
provenance: City of Chicago Landmark Designation Report (2023)

name: The Music Box
claims: Opened February 1983 with Ron Hardy resident.
Address disputed: 1632 S. Indiana (oral histories) vs. Lower Wacker (city report) vs. others. Never state address.
provenance: City of Chicago Landmark Designation Report (2023); CTL-DR-MUSIC-001 timeline

name: The Power Plant
claims: Knuckles's club after the 1983 split with Williams.
provenance: City of Chicago Landmark Designation Report (2023)

name: Hot Mix 5
claims: WBMX mix show 'Saturday Night Live, Ain't No Jive.'
Farley Keith, Mickey 'Mixin' Oliver, Ralphi Rosario, Kenny 'Jammin' Jason, Scott 'Smokin' Silz.
Carried the club sound to ~1M+ weekly radio listeners.

name: Chosen Few DJs
claims: South Side mobile-DJ crew; Chosen Few Picnic from 1990.

name: Trax Records
claims: Pressed key early house records ('Move Your Body,' 'Acid Tracks').
Founding year and credits disputed; 2022 royalty lawsuit (allegations).

name: DJ International Records
claims: Co-founded by Rocky Jones and Benji Espinoza.
Issued Knuckles, Hardy, Farley, Hurley, Jefferson, Fast Eddie releases.

name: WBMX
claims: Chicago station that carried Hot Mix 5 house mixes in the 1980s.

name: Imports Etc.
claims: Dance-music-only record store; DJs' source.
Detroit techno innovators encountered house there (SPIN, 1986).

name: Gramaphone Records
claims: Shifted toward house/DJ vinyl by the 1980s.

name: Jes Say Records
claims: Saunders's label; pressed 'On & On' (Jan 1984).

name: Mitchbal Records
claims: Vince Lawrence's label; released Z-Factor's 'Fantasy' (March 1984).

name: Disco Demolition Night
claims: WLUP/Steve Dahl anti-disco promotion; riot; forfeited game.
Did not 'kill disco' or cause house - context, not cause.

name: 'On & On'
claims: Saunders/Lawrence; generally accepted as first house track committed to vinyl.
Based partly on a Mach 'On & On' bootleg megamix.

name: 'Your Love'
claims: Jamie Principle's song; cassette-circulated in clubs before vinyl.
1987 Trax version credited to Knuckles (disputed).

name: 'Acid Tracks'
claims: Phuture; recorded to tape 1985; club-tested by Hardy.
12-minute TB-303/TR-707/TR-727 instrumental; credited with defining acid house.

name: 'Move Your Body'
claims: Marshall Jefferson; piano-led house anthem.
First-label question (Trax vs DJ International) unresolved.

name: 'Love Can't Turn Around'
claims: Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk; written Lawrence, sung Pandy; UK Top 10.

name: Roland TB-303
claims: Bass Line synthesizer by Tadao Kikumoto; commercial failure; cheap second-hand.
Real-time filter/envelope manipulation = acid house sound.

name: Roland TR-707/TR-727
claims: Digital drum machines used on 'Acid Tracks' alongside the TB-303.

name: Reel-to-reel editing
claims: Knuckles/Levan extended and reworked disco/soul records for the dance floor.

name: Warehouse-era house dance community
claims: Dancers as the scene's social form; queer-of-color congregation.
provenance: City landmark report; Salkind oral histories (via CTL-DR-MUSIC-001)

name: The Fantastic Four
claims: All-female house DJ collective; included DJ Celeste.
